# Healthy for the Holidays: 4 tips to create a Medicare enrollment checklist to help your loved ones


*By **[Whitney Stidom](https://news.ehealthinsurance.com/experts/whitney-stidom)** , vice president of consumer enablement, eHealth*


Millions of families will gather this


fall


to give thanks,


provid


ing


an


ideal


opportunity


to


celebrate while also


check


ing


on the


well-being


of


the loved ones


in your life


.


While


enhancing


our


health


is often focused on exercise and nutrition, it is also important to consider insurance coverage, which


**[research shows](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK221008/)** contributes to well-being through


improve


d


access to preventive


exams


and quality medical care


.


If you


are an adult with


aging parents


or


grandparents


,


this is an important conversation


to have


during


the


fall


’s


Medicare Annual Enrollment Period, when


over 70 million beneficiaries


can


make plan changes for


2027.


In fact,


a


mong American adults with a parent or loved one


enrolled in or


eligible for Medicare,


**[67 % said they have already discussed](https://news.ehealthinsurance.com/_ir/68/202610/d8d82cf80d2213558d3aa98429baa7f6/Medicare_AEP_HalfTime_Report_2026.pdf)**


—


or plan to discuss


—


their loved one's Medicare options


before the Dec. 7


enrollment


deadline


.


This is an important conversation, given


**[71% of Medicare beneficiaries](https://news.ehealthinsurance.com/news/survey-half-of-medicare-beneficiaries-have-skipped-medical-care-in-the-past-year-due-to-confusion-over-their-coverage)** say shopping for a new plan is confusing. To make that


discussion


easier,


here’s


a four-step checklist to help guide


this


conversation with loved one


s


comparing Medicare plans for


next year


.


**1. Review their Annual Notice of Change letter .**


If they have not already done so, confirm they have


reviewed


and understand


their Annual Notice of Change letter, which details how


their existing plan will change for 2027.


These letters are


sent


out


by the end of September,


although


52


% of


Medicare beneficiaries


admit


they


don’t


carefully review


mail from their insurance plan.


If your loved one missed this letter, it is


also available through


the


insurer’s website or app.


**2. Update their healthcare inventory.**


W


ork with your loved one to w


rite down every doctor, specialist


,


fac


il


ity


and prescription


medication


they


use.


Having that list will be important when evaluating


their


Medicare


options


, given


your loved one will want to confirm the plan they select will enable access to their preferred care providers,


facilities


and prescription medications


.


**3. Evaluate their healthcare needs and potential costs.** While


a


Medicare


plan’s


monthly premium is important, it is


also


important to


consider


medi


cal and


prescription drug costs,


deductibles


and potential out-of-pocket exposure in case


of a significant health issue or event. If your loved one is managing a


chronic condition or planning a significant medical procedure in 2027,


it is import


ant to understand what their


financial responsibility


will be each month and throughout the year.


If your loved


one


will


need a lot of care in 2027, it may be better to pay a higher premium in exchange for


a lower deductible or out-of-pocket maximum


.


**4. Help them tap into free resources.** **** There are multiple ways to help your loved one


compare their


Medicare options,


including


Medicare.gov


and the State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP), which provides access to volunteers who can offer general information about Medicare plans. For more personalized guidance, licensed insurance agencies can help


them


compare Medicare plans that can fit your personal health needs, prescriptions, and budget (no obligation to enroll).


***[Whitney Stidom](https://news.ehealthinsurance.com/experts/whitney-stidom)** is vice president of consumer enablement at e Health , an online health insurance marketplace that helps consumers navigate their health benefit decisions*
